abstract: Every SMPTE ST 2110 deployment requires a SMPTE ST 2059/PTP infrastructure. Precision Time Protocol (PTP) systems are complex and have many subtleties. If done well, SMPTE ST 2059/PTP systems can easily be deployed and commissioned. Unfortunately, there are many ways in which system design and commissioning can go wrong, resulting in months or years of unexplained on-air glitches and gremlins. This paper presents the best practices for commissioning SMPTE ST 2059/PTP systems developed from field experiences. This includes practical checklists for both simple designs and advanced PTP over ST 2022-7 networks. Techniques to debug and troubleshoot errors found during commissioning will also be discussed.

authors.bio: Leigh Whitcomb is an architect for Imagine Communications, Toronto, ON, Canada, having joined the company in 1991. He participates in SMPTE, Alliance for IP Media Solutions (AIMS), Insitute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), and Video Services Forum (VSF) standards committees, including serving as co-chair of SMPTE 32NF Network/Facilities Architecture Technology Committee. He is actively involved in SMPTE ST 2110 Professional Media over Managed IP Networks and SMPTE ST 2059 Genlock Over IP. Whitcomb became a SMPTE Fellow in 2017. Since 2017, Whitcomb’s other professional affiliations include VSF, IEEE, and Professional Engineers Ontario. He holds a bachelor’s degree in computer engineering from the University of Waterloo, ON, Canada, and a master’s degree in electrical and computer engineering from the University of Toronto, ON, Canada. He is the co-inventor of several in the areas of networking and timing & synchronization.
